The belt on my dv419aew/xaa worked great right up until it didn't. Very easy to replace.
1. Have a vacuum ready.
2. Unplug
3. Pull top off
4. Pull front off
5. Pull blower cover off
6. Pull drum off
7. Put everything back on with new belt
8. On back, take out three screws to pull out dryer vent
9. Put belt on as shown in picture
10. Rotate drum a few times to make sure its on
11. Put back together, plug in, success!

Wanted to try a Refresh brand filter because the price was reasonable. I'm giving this filter a tentative 5 star rating because it fit perfectly in our LG refrigerator. The initial few gallons of water did have a "gray" look because of small carbon particles but it quickly cleared up as expected. This is quite typical of carbon filters.

But, since filter performance can only be judged on flow rate, color, taste ,smell and longevity I'll need to wait a few months for my final assessment.
Being the nerdy guy I am, I have already cut open a genuine, used LG filter to check out construction. I'll do the same with the Refresh filter after I finally remove it. My expectation is it will also be a typical carbon block design and will be just fine.
UPDATE: Okay, I did cut open the used Refresh brand filter and found it to be constructed well, as expected. In some ways ( for example the internal water flow channels ) I thought the design was better than the more expensive LG filter. Otherwise, the Refresh filter uses a typical carbon block to achieve good performance. I'll keep using them. A good value.

No No NO. Just spend a few more dollars and buy the OEM replacement. The frustration I had trying to replace my water filter on my LG refrigerator was a nightmare. Although it looked about right in a side by side comparison to the original filter I had, it was NOT!!! I followed directions to the "t" and when I did a test run by running out the water for a few gallons (per the directions), the filter started to leak inside of the fridge. I thought I installed it wrong, I must have taken it out and put it back in 10 times, and every time it would leak and make a hissing sound. So, something that I thought would take a few minutes to install, caused me to spend a good hour in the kitchen trying to reinstall while cleaning up all the water that flooded my fridge. Nightmare! I sent the product back to Amazon right away and reordered the OEM filter by LG and was able to pop in it the fridge in a matter of seconds and it worked like a charm. No problems whatsoever!

This filter is not a replacement for the LT500P.  Although it appears to fit, it does not seal, and I had a huge mess to clean up when the water leaked out.  My LG refrigerator is model LSC27925ST.  This filter may work in others, but not in mine, although it was listed as a replacement .

At first I would have given this product a 4-5 stars, just due to ease of install, but after over a week of having the product installed, the quality is no where near the LG one I replaced.
After install I pulled roughly 3 gallons of water through the filter, as I have with any other filter I have owned, but the water still has an odd taste, and additionally after the ice melts in bottle there is sediment and hard water stains all over the inside. So, I'm not fully sure what this filter does other than take up the space in the back of my fridge.
If Refresh has a better install plan that would be awesome, but please don't market yourself as equal to the OEM.
